t: This is the National Police Memorial in central London, which remembers about four thousand police officers killed in the course of their duties across the United Kingdom. It was unveiled in 2005. Two people shaped it. The architect Norman Foster, a leading figure in British high-tech modernism, designed it, and the Danish designer and artist Per Arnoldi made it. Arnoldi works across painting, sculpture, ceramics and monuments, and his pieces are held in the Museum of Modern Art in New York. Take a moment here to think about the officers it honours.
